title: Power Failure / The World Answers by Going Dark

source_refs.author: Horror and thriller staging tradition
source_refs.title: Electrical failure as a world reply
source_refs.cultural_context: Narrative cinema in which a blackout is timed to an event and may return later

observed_structure: Practical sources define what can be seen.
Those sources fail on the peak of an event, not at a random moment.
The same failure can return later, so the dark is a motif and not a one-time effect.
dramatic_operations: drop practical illumination as the world answers an event
let darkness arrive on a sonic peak rather than as a random outage
allow the same failure to recur later as a motif
cinematic_affordances: a small set of practicals established before they die
the cut or the outage landed on an audio peak
a beat of black before a reduced image returns
a later recurrence of the same failure with a changed stake
cultural_scope: general electrical-failure motif; do not claim a supernatural grid without project rules
misuse_risks: a blackout used only to hide a missing effect
killing the lights with no established practicals
a single outage that never returns and therefore carries no motif

variables: what is different when the image returns

transferable_structure: a power failure answers the scene on a peak and can return later as the world's repeated reply
non_transferable_surface: a copied blackout gag, flicker pattern, or generator stunt from a specific film
